physical_barriers.name: Anti-Infiltration Obstacle System (AIOS)
physical_barriers.temporal_variations: Constructed 2003-2005; smart fence integration underway with sensors; hybrid model adoption due to cost; 60 km smart fence attempted in 2020 [citation:11]
physical_barriers.stated_justification: Government of India justifies the LoC fencing and security measures as necessary to prevent infiltration from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and terrorist attacks. The fence forms the first line of defense in a three-tier counter-infiltration grid. The smart fence enhancement was motivated by the Pathankot and Uri terror attacks in which terrorists crossed the LoC [citation:4].
physical_barriers.opposing_characterization: Local Kashmiri advocates characterize the fence as a tool of partition and separation, restricting movement and livelihoods; security checkpoints are seen as obstacles to civilian freedom.

water_infrastructure.name: Indus River (Indus Waters Treaty)
water_infrastructure.capacity_or_flow_rate: Part of Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan; western rivers allocated to Pakistan under the 1960 treaty. India has only constructed 3,482 MW capacity out of an estimated 20,000 MW potential from hydro-power generation units on western rivers [citation:10].

water_infrastructure.name: Jhelum River
water_infrastructure.controlling_entity: Government of India / J&K State Power Development Corporation

water_infrastructure.name: Chenab River
water_infrastructure.capacity_or_flow_rate: 390 MW Dulhasti Power Station operational since 2007; 260 MW Dulhasti Stage-II approved for construction; 1,856 MW Sawalkot hydroelectric project approved in 2025 [citation:3][citation:10]. The Dulhasti Stage-II project is likely to become the first hydropower project on a western river to be completed after India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: Five-judge Constitution Bench unanimously upheld the Central government's 2019 decision to abrogate Article 370. Key holdings include: J&K did not retain internal sovereignty; Article 370 is a temporary provision; the President had the power to notify abrogation without State Assembly concurrence; the J&K Constitution is now inoperative; elections to be held by September 30, 2024 [citation:5][citation:12]. Justice S.K. Kaul recommended an impartial Truth and Reconciliation Commission to investigate human rights violations since the 1980s [citation:5].
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: The Court accepted the Union's argument that Article 370 was a temporary provision meant to serve a transitional purpose. The Union government defended its decision, stating there was no constitutional fraud in repealing the provision, and that after the changes, street violence orchestrated by terrorists and secessionist networks has become a thing of the past [citation:1][citation:5].

landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.holding_or_standard: Bifurcated the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories: Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh, effective October 31, 2019 [citation:1][citation:2].
landmark_jurisprudence_and_treaties.official_legal_rationale: The government stated that the reorganisation was necessary for administrative efficiency and development. The Solicitor General stated that the Union Territory of J&K would be returned to statehood as soon as possible [citation:5].

documented_statutory_conflicts.enforced_clause_reference: Central legislation amendments opening land ownership to non-domiciles
documented_statutory_conflicts.preferred_or_prior_clause_reference: 1938 J&K Alienation of Land Act, Big Land Estates Abolition Act of 1950 (pre-existing state laws)
documented_statutory_conflicts.conflict_description: Prior to 2019, Article 35A restricted land ownership in J&K to permanent residents. The revocation of Article 370 allowed central laws to apply, effectively superseding the 1938 J&K Alienation of Land Act and Big Land Estates Abolition Act of 1950. This allows non-domicile individuals to purchase land in the UT.

documented_statutory_conflicts.preferred_or_prior_clause_reference: Previous constitutional framework granting special status and autonomy
documented_statutory_conflicts.conflict_description: The Central government's revocation of the special status is contested by local advocates who consider the 2019 act unconstitutional, arguing it bypassed the requirement for State concurrence and undermined the historical autonomy of the region.

official_threat_assessments_or_attack_st.description: Infiltration attempts and terrorist attacks cited by Indian security forces
official_threat_assessments_or_attack_st.numbers_or_incidents: The Pathankot and Uri terror attacks in 2016, in which terrorists crossed the LoC, motivated the smart fence enhancement [citation:4]. The 2025 Pahalgam terror attack prompted the government to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty and accelerate hydropower projects [citation:10]. The Central government stated that after the revocation of Article 370, street violence, which was engineered and orchestrated by terrorists and secessionist networks, has become a thing of the past [citation:1].
official_threat_assessments_or_attack_st.citation: The Hindu, 2017; Times of India, 2025; Zee News, 2023

official_threat_assessments_or_attack_st.description: Detention under Public Safety Act and AFSPA
official_threat_assessments_or_attack_st.numbers_or_incidents: According to state government figures, 4,064 people were arrested from March 2010 to January 2011 under the PSA and AFSPA, with 3,900 released. Amnesty International estimated between 8,000 and 20,000 people have been detained under the PSA or AFSPA over the past 20 years [citation:14].

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.measure: Revocation of Article 370 and bifurcation of J&K
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Necessary for administrative efficiency, development, and complete integration with the Indian Union. The Central government defended its decision, stating there was no constitutional fraud and that after the changes, street violence orchestrated by terrorists and secessionist networks has become a thing of the past [citation:1]. The Solicitor General stated that statehood of J&K will be restored except for the carving out of Ladakh [citation:5].
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.citation: Government of India statements; Supreme Court verdict 2023

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.measure: LoC fencing and smart fence enhancement
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Prevent infiltration from Pakistan and terrorist attacks. The fence is the first line of defense in the three-tier counter-infiltration grid. The smart fence was motivated by the Pathankot and Uri terror attacks in which terrorists crossed the LoC [citation:4].

stated_administrative_or_security_ration.measure: AFSPA, Public Safety Act, and UAPA
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.official_rationale: Security legislation necessary to maintain public order, prevent terrorism, and protect national security. The use of these acts is justified as a response to ongoing security threats and militant activity.
stated_administrative_or_security_ration.opposing_characterization: Local advocates characterize AFSPA as a 'lawless law' that enables security forces to act with impunity. Under AFSPA, prosecution of security personnel requires central government sanction, which is practically impossible - until July 2018, the union government denied permission to prosecute in all 50 cases sent for sanction [citation:7]. From March 2010 to January 2011, 4,064 people were arrested under PSA/AFSPA; Amnesty International estimates 8,000-20,000 people detained over 20 years [citation:14].
